title: K-theory of number fields and S-integers, Part II
summary: A complete target-level planning pass for symplectic K-theory of Z, CM generation, and its finite, p-adic and locally split universal Galois extensions. 42 targets extend ArithmeticKTheory while importing the generic spectral, Hermitian, CM, moduli and étale-realization owners. The characteristic-number application uses strict prime bounds and the repaired Hurewicz range. Explicit supplier requests and three gaps keep planned coverage distinct from a closed proof plan.
readme: A continuation from arithmetic K-groups and their étale descriptions to symplectic K-theory of Z and its Galois action. The reader document states every target, hypothesis, API, Check and supplier boundary. All nine layers are planned; three explicit gaps and open interface requests remain. No result is claimed implemented.

stages.title: Cyclotomic Bott and Picard classes
stages.description: Universal cyclic Bott class: For odd q, the Bockstein followed by Hurewicz identifies π₂(Σ∞₊B(Z/q);Z/q) with H₁(B(Z/q);Z)=Z/q. Let β_q correspond to 1. Its image in connective complex K-theory under the tautological character is the Bott generator in degree two. Raising the character to a∈(Z/q)× sends β_q to aβ_q. For q>4 its powers generate a split polynomial subalgebra (Z/q)[β_q] in stable homotopy; at q=3 only iterated Bott maps from the supplier contract are used. Picard-to-K map: For a commutative ring R, specialize the imported Picard-groupoid construction to invertible R-modules, isomorphisms, and tensor product. Its components are Mathlib’s CommRing.Pic R and its unit automorphisms are R×. The tensor functor to projective modules gives a multiplicative map Σ∞₊|Pic(R)|→K(R), using K.7’s coherent tensor product separately from additive group completion. For a Dedekind domain, representatives by fractional ideals give morphisms from I to J by a∈Frac(R)× satisfying aI=J; these are not restricted to R×. Cyclotomic Picard classes: Put K_q=Q(ζ_q), O_q=Z[ζ_q] and O′_q=O_q[1/p]. For k≥1 the map (Pic(O_q)/q)⊗μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}→K_{4k−2}(O_q;Z/q)^(+) sending [L]⊗ζ_q^{⊗(2k−1)} to β(ζ_q)^{2k−1}([L]−1) is an isomorphism onto the positive eigensummand. For all k∈Z the same formula in Bott-inverted K-theory is an isomorphism. Inverting p does not change this Picard group because the unique prime over p is principal. These identifications are Galois-equivariant; ψ⁻¹ acts by +1 on the target. Cyclotomic transfer descent: For every k∈Z, transfer induces an isomorphism (K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O′_q;Z/q)^(+))_{Gal(K_q/Q)}≅K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z[1/p];Z/q)^(+). There is the parallel isomorphism in degree 4k for the negative eigensummand. In the positive comparison range these identify ordinary groups over O_q and Z. Transfer commutes with the duality involution here after accounting for the inverse different, whose ideal class is principal. Artin–Bott transfer square: Let H_q/K_q be the maximal everywhere-unramified abelian p-extension inside C, and G_q=Gal(H_q/Q). Arithmetic Artin reciprocity identifies Pic(O_q)⊗Z_p with Gal(H_q/K_q). For every k∈Z and M_q=μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}, the Artin/Bott identifications and transfer give a commuting square from H₁(Gal(H_q/K_q);M_q) to K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O_q;Z/q)^(+) and from H₁(G_q;M_q) to K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)^(+). Its vertical arrows are group-homology pushforward and K-transfer. The bottom map is an isomorphism; H₁(G_q;M_q)≅H₁(G_q,⟨c⟩;M_q), where c is complex conjugation.

stages.title: Betti–Hodge maps and Bott inversion
stages.description: Betti and Hodge maps: Use H.4’s symplectic group completion of finite free unimodular alternating Z-modules, with basepoint component BSp∞(Z)⁺, as KSp(Z). Define c_B:KSp(Z)→K(Z) by forgetting the form. Define c_H:KSp(Z)→ku using Sp(Z)→Sp(R)^top←U^top and the homotopy equivalence on the right. On topological complex K-theory ψ⁻¹ is complex conjugation. Hermitian forms are linear in their first variable; the Hodge complex structure is fixed by the condition that its imaginary Hermitian pairing equals the supplied alternating form. Bott-inverted symplectic K-theory: For q=p^n choose the compatible Adams v₁ self-map on a mod-q Moore spectrum of degree m=2p^{n−1}(p−1) supplied by H.6, and let T_q be its telescope. Put KSp^{(β)}(Z;Z/q)=KSp(Z)∧T_q, with the associated ordinary-to-periodic map. Define the Z_p version by the homotopy inverse limit over the coefficient tower. The Betti and Hodge maps extend to K^{(β)} and KU. The q=3 construction uses an iterated self-map, with no associative Moore-ring assumption.

stages.title: CM coefficient lines and prescribed types
stages.description: Hermitian coefficient-line groupoids: For a CM field E, maximal order O with conjugation, and an invertible O-module ω with semilinear involution ι, let P(O,ω,ι) have invertible O-modules L with a perfect O-linear pairing b:L⊗_O bar L≅ω such that swapping the two factors agrees with ι. Arrows are O-linear isometries. Set P⁺=P(O,O,conjugation) and P⁻=P(O,ω_{O/Z},−conjugation), where the inverse different is the trace-dual line. Tensoring coefficient lines gives P⁺ an action on P⁻. A P⁻ object has a CM type determined by the signs of Im τ(b(x,x)), x≠0. This specializes CM.2’s polarized lattices; it is not another definition of CM lattices. Trace polarization and CM realization: There is a functor ST:P⁻_E→A_g(C) with g=[E:Q]/2. It sends (L,b) to the principally polarized CM abelian variety obtained from the symplectic lattice (L_Z,−Tr_{E/Q}b) and its unique compatible complex structure of type Φ(L,b). The positive Hermitian form is h(x,y)=−2i Σ_{τ∈Φ}τ b(x,y), with Im h=−Tr b. For this linear-first convention, ω(v,J_H v)=−h(v,v); hence the compatible almost-complex structure in Tau Ceti’s convention is −J_H for ω=Im h. Equivalently J_H is compatible with −ω. This sign adapter is required before invoking exists_compatible. The O-action is faithful and its Rosati involution restricts to conjugation. ST identifies P⁻ with the rank-one projective O-homology locus of CM.2’s classification. For a positive Hermitian O-line X, ST(L⊗X)≅ST(L)⊗_O X compatibly with polarization; (O,−1) gives complex conjugation. Split primes with prescribed signs: For E=K_q and E⁺ its real subfield, any sign function on the real embeddings of E⁺ is realized by t∈O_{E⁺} whose principal ideal is a prime away from p splitting in E, so (t)O_E=x bar x for a prime ideal x of O_E. The narrow Hilbert class field used in the proof is the full narrow class field of E⁺, distinct from the p-Hilbert field H_q. CM types and ideal differences: For q odd, every CM type Φ on K_q and every invertible ideal L of O_q admit B₁,B₂∈P⁻_{K_q}, both of type Φ, whose underlying ideal classes satisfy [B₁][B₂]^{−1}=[L][bar L]^{−1}. Thus all types occur, while prescribed anti-conjugate ideal differences can be realized without changing the Hodge type.

stages.title: CM generation and the Betti–Hodge computation
stages.description: CM Bott classes: For (L,b)∈P⁻_{K_q} and k≥1, let z_{L,b}=β_q^{2k−1}[L,b]∈KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q). Here β acts through the specified μ_q subgroup of norm-one automorphisms, the unreduced stable nerve of P⁻, and its trace-form map to KSp. Products are supplied as iterated maps at q=3. Tensoring positive lines acts through this stable construction; a class [L,b] is in degree zero and its Bott translate has degree 4k−2. Hodge type character formula: If Φ⊂(Z/q)× is the type of (L,b), then c_H(β_q^i[L,b])=(Σ_{a∈Φ}a^i)·bott^i in π_{2i}(ku;Z/q). For odd i, the span of these scalars as Φ varies is all Z/q: changing the choice in one conjugate pair changes the sum by ±2a^i, a unit. Consequently c_H:KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)→Z/q is onto for k≥1, independently of the Betti–Hodge splitting theorem. Betti transfer formula: For (L,b)∈P⁻_{K_q}, c_B(z_{L,b})=tr_{O_q/Z}(β(ζ_q)^{2k−1}([L]−1)). This depends only on L. The term tr(β^{2k−1}) vanishes because conjugation acts with sign −1 on the odd Bott power whereas transfer lands in the positive eigensummand. Betti–Hodge splitting theorem: For i≥0 and q odd, (p_+c_B,p_-c_H):KSp_i(Z;Z/q)≅K_i(Z;Z/q)^(+)⊕π_i(ku;Z/q)^(−), where p_±=(1±ψ⁻¹)/2. In degree 4k−2, k≥1, this is K_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)⊕Z/q, with the arithmetic term identified with H²_et(Z[1/p];μ_q^{⊗2k}). For i>0 the p-adic groups vanish for i≡0,1 mod4, are K_i(Z;Z_p)⊕Z_p for i≡2 mod4, and are K_i(Z;Z_p) for i≡3 mod4. The direct-sum splitting is an abelian-group assertion, not a Galois-equivariant splitting of the main extension. CM classes generate symplectic K-theory: For every odd q and k≥1, the map π^s_{4k−2}(|P⁻_{K_q}|;Z/q)→KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q) is onto. For an ideal L, choose pairs of CM lines for L and O_q having a common type. The four-class difference has zero Hodge image and Betti image 2·tr(β^{2k−1}([L]−1)). The arithmetic transfer is onto and 2 is a unit; combine these kernel generators with one Hodge-unit combination. Periodic and K(1)-local comparison: The Betti–Hodge map for KSp^{(β)} gives KSp^{(β)}_i(Z;Z/q)≅K^{(β)}_i(Z;Z/q)^(+)⊕π_i(KU;Z/q)^(−) for every integer i. For i≥0 it agrees with connective KSp. After p-completion this periodic spectrum is L_{K(1)}KSp(Z), with the localization comparison specified by H.6’s telescope contract. The analogous comparison for algebraic K-theory is imported; the exceptional degree-one comparison over Z is retained there.

stages.title: Arithmetic ppav realization and spectrum action
stages.description: Polarized abelian Γ-groupoid: For a finite pointed set T, define A(T) from principally polarized abelian varieties (A,λ) and a unital ring map φ:Z^T→End(A) whose image is fixed by the Rosati involution defined by λ. Put e=1−e_* and select eA. Arrows are polarized isomorphisms of selected factors commuting with the Z^T-action. For f:T→U, restriction along f*:Z^U→Z^T defines the Γ map. The stack is equivalent to (∐_{g≥0}A_g)^{T\{*}}. This is a ppav specialization of H.4’s Γ construction and the imported ppav moduli stack, not a second generic Γ-space. Rigidified ppav simplicial model: Rigidify the selected factor in A(T) by a projective embedding from the third power of the ample line bundle Δ*L, where L represents the principal polarization correspondence. Let U(T) be the coproduct of the resulting quasi-projective parameter schemes over embedding dimension and Hilbert polynomial. Its Čech nerve Z(T)_r has r+1 embeddings together with compatible isomorphisms of their ppav objects. It is a specified coproduct of quasi-projective simplicial schemes over Q, graded by dimension vectors. The construction is Γ-functorial through the imported product/rigidification coherence contract; it does not claim the entire unbounded coproduct is one quasi-projective scheme. Betti model of symplectic K-theory: The analytic ppav stack of genus g is H_g//Sp_{2g}(Z), where Siegel space H_g is contractible. Its Betti realization is therefore weakly equivalent to BSp_{2g}(Z). Level N≥4 gives a smooth finite-level atlas; quotient singular complexes are compared by weak equivalences, not literal simplicial isomorphisms. For every finite pointed T, Sing_an Z_C(T)≃N SP_T(Z) naturally as special Γ-spaces; at S⁰ this is ∐_g BSp_{2g}(Z). Applying the existing Segal machine gives KSp(Z). Galois action on the symplectic spectrum: Algebraic conjugation sends a complex ppav with structure map φ to the same underlying scheme with structure map Spec(σ⁻¹)∘φ, and transports its polarization and arrows. This gives a left Aut(C)-action: σ·(τ·A)=(στ)·A. For an odd prime p, use componentwise graded p-completed étale realization of the Q-defined Z(T), with EH.6’s comparison, to obtain a homotopy-coherent Aut(C)-action by spectrum maps on KSp(Z)^∧_p and compatible mod-p^n spectra. For p>3 the vanishing of H₁(A_g;F_p) allows the direct finite-type comparison on each genus. For p=3 first smash each connected component, pointed by a rational ppav, with the simply connected Moore space M(Z/p^n,2), realize this simplicially, compare, then desuspend twice and pass through the tower. Naturality includes the discrete complex-point map. The action is independent, up to the supplied coherent equivalences, of rigidifications and basepoint choices. Finite-genus detection of the action: For q odd, k≥1 and g≥φ(q), the map π^s_{4k−2}(|A_g(C)^δ|;Z/q)→KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q) is onto and equivariant for the action just constructed. This conservative bound suffices: CM objects have genus φ(q)/2 and can be stabilized to g by a rational principally polarized abelian variety. The q-level action is uniquely determined by equivariance of all discrete ppav maps in these degrees. Complex conjugation fixes c_B; the Hodge twist is established by CM formulas in AK2.5.

stages.title: Relative extensions and CM reciprocity
stages.description: Groupoid CM reciprocity formula: Let E/Q be a Galois CM field with full Hilbert class field H. Choose lifts w_τ:H→C of τ:E→C with w_{cτ}=c w_τ=w_τ c. Transport of a CM line of type Φ by σ∈Aut(C) has type σΦ and is tensoring by a positive Hermitian line (X,h), depending only on σ and Φ. Under arithmetic Artin reciprocity its ideal class is represented by ∏_{τ∈Φ} w_{στ}^{−1}σw_τ∈Gal(H/E). The functorial comparison with ST and Serre tensor respects polarization and O-action. The formula is in Gal(H/E); H_q denotes the p-subfield only after specialization. Split extension category: For a commutative ring Λ, group G, subgroup H and left Λ[G]-module M, let C_Λ(G,H;M) have objects (V,π,s) with π:V→M a surjective G-linear map, trivial G-action on T=ker π, and an H-linear section s:M→V with π∘s=id_M. A morphism f is G-linear, satisfies π′f=π and fs=s′, and may induce any Λ-linear map on kernels. The unsectioned category C_Λ(G;M) remembers only (V,π). The H-split subcategory of that category forgets the chosen section. Relative bar convention comparison: For the relative chain complex C_*(G,H;M)=C_*(G;M)/C_*(H;Res M) imported from R02.2, construct its FGV left-coefficient presentation and comparison. It has C₀=0 and H₁ presented by generators [g]⊗m, linear in m, relations [h]⊗m=0 for h∈H and [gg′]⊗m=[g]⊗g′m+[g′]⊗m. Supply an explicit natural chain equivalence with Mathlib’s inhomogeneous-chain convention, whose differential uses inverse actions, before invoking its groupHomology. The canonical α_univ(g,m)=[g]⊗m is a relative 1-cycle class. Universal relative extension: There is an equivalence C_Λ(G,H;M)≃(H₁(G,H;M)↓Mod_Λ). Its initial object has underlying module M⊕H₁(G,H;M), projection to M, section m↦(m,0), and action g·(m,t)=(g·m,t+[g]⊗m). Every extension is its pushout through the unique cocycle-induced kernel map. If H₀(H;M)=H₁(H;M)=0, forgetting the section is an equivalence to C_Λ(G;M); if only H₀ vanishes, it is an equivalence to its H-split subcategory. In this roadmap these forgetful assertions are used for finite free M and H=⟨c⟩ with c acting by −1 over an odd-primary coefficient ring.

stages.title: The finite universal Galois extension
stages.description: Finite arithmetic Galois action: For q odd and k≥1, the spectrum action on V_q=KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q) factors through G_q=Gal(H_q/Q). The Hodge map gives an exact G_q-sequence 0→T_q→V_q→M_q→0 with M_q=μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}, trivial action on T_q, and T_q≅K_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q). The restriction c_H:ker c_B→M_q is an isomorphism and its inverse is the unique ⟨c⟩-equivariant splitting. The Hodge map has weight 2k−1; the Betti map is only conjugation-invariant on V_q. CM reciprocity identifies the universal cocycle: Give the extension V_q the ⟨c⟩-section s=(c_H|ker c_B)^{-1}. Its cocycle α(σ,m)=σs(m)−s(σm) defines H₁(G_q,⟨c⟩;M_q)→T_q. Under the Artin–Bott transfer isomorphism of AK2.0 this map is the identity. Explicitly a CM type Φ supplies the coefficient (Σ_{a∈Φ}a^{2k−1}) and reciprocity supplies the product of lift differences; their relative-bar class is [σ] times that coefficient. Equality is in homology modulo boundaries and the ⟨c⟩-chains. Finite-coefficient universal extension theorem: For odd p, q=p^n and k≥1, the arithmetic sequence 0→K_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)→KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)→μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}→0 is initial in C_{Z/q}(G_q,⟨c⟩;μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) and in the unsectioned category C_{Z/q}(G_q;μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}). Its kernel is canonically H₁(G_q,⟨c⟩;μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) through Artin–Bott transfer. The inclusion of the arithmetic K group is the inverse of c_B on the Hodge kernel; relative to the standard hyperbolic H on this positive summand it is (1/2)H.

stages.title: Continuous, local and all-twist extensions
stages.description: Continuous universal extensions: Let Γ be a profinite group, H a closed subgroup and M a finite free Z_p-module with continuous action. In C^cts_{Z_p}(Γ,H;M), objects and morphisms are the continuous counterparts of AK2.5 with finitely generated p-complete kernel and middle module and a continuous H-section. Completed relative homology is computed by the completed bar complex, equivalently the inverse system over open normal U and coefficient powers p^n with the induced pair and coefficient coinvariants. For the Γ and G occurring below, finite-coefficient homology is finite and the resulting H₁ is finitely generated; thus its completed universal extension is initial in this category. Surjective finite towers remove the relevant lim¹ obstruction. p-adic universal extension theorem: Let H_∞=∪_{n≥1}H_{p^n} and Γ=Gal(H_∞/Q). For k≥1 the spectrum action gives a continuous exact sequence 0→K_{4k−2}(Z;Z_p)→KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z_p)→Z_p(2k−1)→0. The arithmetic kernel is finite with trivial Γ-action. With its unique conjugation-equivariant section it is initial in C^cts_{Z_p}(Γ,⟨c⟩;Z_p(2k−1)); forgetting that section gives initiality in the unsectioned category of finite-type compact continuous extensions. Its kernel is H₁^cts(Γ,⟨c⟩;Z_p(2k−1)). Local splitting and relative homology: Let Q(p) be the maximal extension of Q unramified outside p, G=Gal(Q(p)/Q), and choose a c-fixed prime above p, giving a decomposition subgroup G_𝔭. Choose it compatibly in H_∞; let D_q⊂G_q be its image. The natural map of pairs (G,G_𝔭)→(G_q,D_q) induces H₁^cts(G,G_𝔭;M_q)≅H₁(G_q,D_q;M_q)≅H₁(G_q,⟨c⟩;M_q). Here D_q≅Gal(K_q/Q) because the principal prime above p splits in H_q/K_q. The KSp extension is uniquely D_q-split and its section has image ker c_B. Universal locally split Galois extension: For odd p and k≥1, the sequence of AK2.7/padic-universality, inflated to G, has a unique G_𝔭-equivariant splitting with image ker c_B and is initial in C^cts_{Z_p}(G,G_𝔭;Z_p(2k−1)). Equivalently its associated lisse Z_p-sheaf on Spec Z[1/p] is the universal extension of Z_p(2k−1) by a constant finite-type Z_p-sheaf whose pullback to Spec Q_p is split. Its kernel is H₁^cts(G,G_𝔭;Z_p(2k−1)). Bott-inverted universal extension theorem: For every integer k, including k≤0, replace the K and KSp groups in the finite, p-adic and local universal extensions by their Bott-inverted versions. Their quotients remain μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)} or Z_p(2k−1), and all three initiality statements hold in the same coefficient categories. At finite q one may move k to a positive integer using a compatible period for both the group and cyclotomic twist. Then pass to the p-adic limit; this passage does not make the Z_p groups periodic. Trivial action in degree 4k−1: For p odd and k≥1, Aut(C) acts trivially on KSp_{4k−1}(Z;Z_p). The sphere-unit map π^s_{4k−1}(S;Z_p)→K_{4k−1}(Z;Z_p) is onto, by Quillen’s finite-field comparison at an auxiliary prime ℓ topologically generating Z_p×. The symplectic unit made from a rational elliptic curve maps under c_B to twice that unit. Since c_B is an isomorphism in this degree and 2 is invertible, the rational symplectic unit is onto and is Galois-fixed. Vandiver and conjugation-fixed primes: For q=p^n, the primes of H_q above p form a torsor under Gal(H_q/K_q). After choosing a c-fixed prime, c acts on this torsor by its action on that p-class group. Thus there is exactly one c-fixed prime precisely when its plus part is zero; under the Iwasawa control interface this is equivalent to Vandiver(p). This assertion concerns c-fixed primes. The entire prime set is a singleton only when the full p-class group vanishes, the regular-prime condition.

stages.title: Stable integral homology and characteristic numbers
stages.description: Integral homology indecomposables: For a connected H-space X of finite type, let I=H_{>0}(X;Z_p) be the augmentation ideal and I_r=H_{>0}(X;Z/p^r). Let β_r:H_j(X;Z/p^r)→H_{j−1}(X;Z_p) be the coefficient Bockstein. Put D=I²+Σ_{r≥1}β_r(I_r²), the Z_p-submodule of integral decomposables, and Q^int_*(X)=I/D. Products in the squares have both factors in strictly positive degree; D is not the indecomposable quotient itself. Coefficients here are ordinary singular homology with Z_p on an integral finite-type X. Product formula for integral indecomposables: For connected H-spaces X,Y with finitely generated integral homology in every degree, inclusions and projections give Q^int_i(X×Y)≅Q^int_i(X)⊕Q^int_i(Y). Positive tensor products vanish in I². A Künneth Tor generator from p^r- and p^s-torsion factors is β_d(xy), d=min(r,s), and vanishes in the enlarged denominator. This is an integral product assertion, not a rationalization argument. Low-range integral Hurewicz theorem: Let p be odd and E a spectrum with π_i(E)=0 for i≤0 and finitely generated integral homotopy groups in every degree. Put X=Ω∞E. For 1≤i≤2p−3, the Hurewicz quotient π_i(E)⊗Z_p→Q^int_i(X) is an isomorphism. This repaired statement uses an integral finite-type spectrum, not arbitrary p-complete E with ordinary discrete Z_p-homology. The printed endpoint i=2p−2 is a distinct unresolved target G2; it is not part of this theorem. Integral stable symplectic comparison: Let p be odd. For 1≤i≤2p−3, the stable Hurewicz quotient KSp_i(Z)⊗Z_p→Q^int_i(BSp∞(Z)) is an isomorphism and is Aut(C)-equivariant for the arithmetic action from the ppav model. Stabilization is used in the conservative range g>2i+5. In even degree i=2m in this range, the primitive Hodge class ch_m(ω), with m<p, pairs through this quotient and corresponds to c_H after the usual topological Bott normalization. The primitive condition kills products; its integral lift and Bockstein compatibility kill the enlarged denominator. Rational stable Hodge generators: The stable rational p-adic cohomology of Sp_{2g}(Z) is Q_p[x₂,x₆,x₁₀,…], with primitive generator x_{4k−2} represented by the normalized odd Hodge Chern character ch_{2k−1}(ω). Its arithmetic action is cyclotomic weight 2k−1 in cohomology with the convention that x_{4k−2} is fixed as a class in H^{4k−2}(−;Q_p(2k−1)); the untwisted class therefore has inverse cyclotomic character. Products have the sum of the weights. The rational algebra calculation and stability are imported from BorelRegulators; the identification with the ppav action is the new comparison here. Bernoulli divisibility for ppav families: Let X/Q be smooth projective of dimension d, and A→X a principally polarized abelian scheme with Hodge bundle ω=Lie(A/X)^∨. For a partition d=n₁+⋯+n_r into positive odd integers and an odd prime p>max_j n_j, suppose p divides the numerator of the arithmetic Bernoulli number B_{n_i+1} for some i. Then s=∫_{X(C)}∏_j ch_{n_j}(ω) belongs to p Z_(p). The strict prime inequality makes all Chern-character factorial denominators units. The boundary case p=max n_j is recorded as G3, not included in the result.
